title: Vibrations, waves and sound
scope: Use your school’s topic list to select the ideas you need. These are original practice questions with illustrative values and suggested self-marking guidance, not official Cambridge papers.

objectives.label: Calculate period and frequency and evaluate pendulum timing methods.
objectives.note: Use cycles per second and time per cycle; explain why timing repeated small swings reduces relative reaction-time uncertainty.

objectives.label: Explain resonance, driving frequency and the effect of damping.
objectives.note: Link repeated energy input to a favourable phase near resonance; explain why damping limits amplitude.

objectives.label: Distinguish wave travel from particle motion and calculate wave speed.
objectives.note: Use v = fλ; identify oscillation and propagation directions, including transverse-wave examples.

objectives.label: Explain sound propagation and calculate distances from echoes.
objectives.note: Describe compressions and rarefactions, explain the need for a medium, and count both legs of an echo journey.

objectives.label: Use sound traces to distinguish pitch from loudness.
objectives.note: Compare cycle spacing and amplitude separately; recognise that frequency data alone cannot establish loudness.

objectives.label: Explain timbre, nodes and how vibration modes affect musical sounds.
objectives.note: Relate overtone mixtures to timbre, identify zero-amplitude nodes, and explain effects of string tension and tabla loading.

objectives.label: Explain sound Doppler shifts using wavefront arrival rates.
objectives.note: Distinguish emitted from observed frequency and specify source and observer velocities relative to the medium.

cards.definition: A large driven response near a system’s natural frequency.

cards.confusion: Sound does not propagate through a vacuum.

cards.explanation: Relative source-observer motion can change the observed frequency. The source need not change its emitted frequency.

questions.title: Sound · Complete the method
questions.prompt: A model sound wave has frequency 220.0 Hz and wavelength 1.60 m. Calculate its speed to three significant figures.
points: Use v = fλ.
v = 220.0 × 1.60 = 352 m/s to three significant figures.
model: Use v = fλ.
v = 220.0 × 1.60 = 352 m/s to three significant figures.
accepted: Accept 352 m/s, including equivalent three-significant-figure notation. Award the relationship mark separately from the final result.
questions.common: Sound does not propagate through a vacuum.
hints: A mechanical wave of pressure and density changes travelling through a medium.
